title: Soviet & Cold War-era cinematic music made with Suno - came out better than I expected
author: _AssetSmithy_
selftext:
I used Suno to put together a Soviet / USSR-era cinematic set for game music - everyday life, state parades and Cold War tension.  
  
The warm "everyday life" tracks surprised me most (a quiet love theme, a marketplace, a workplace routine) - nostalgic and unmistakably Soviet without tipping into parody. Curious what you all think of Suno for period moods like this.

Btw, I used Claude to write the Suno prompts.

comments.author: Grandrcp
comments.body: Quite insteresting, although it sounds like a group of jazz musicians gathered in 2010 to record soviet songs, you know? Doesn'

comments.author: Grandrcp
comments.body: I am developing a game staged in USSR, are you also working on something like this? I'd be nice to share some ideas.

replies.author: _AssetSmithy_
replies.body:
It's probably also due to the clean sound. There's barely any clean Soviet music from the 60s and 70s. But I have to say, the music itself fits well. Afterwards I listened to a few original tracks on YouTube – sounds similar.

Regarding the game/project: No, I'm not working on any games or projects. But I create 2D backgrounds, icons and avatars for things like Visual Novels or Battleback RPG, depending on what you want to use them for.
